data.body: **P2 — Contain rejected asynchronous factory results.** Runtime validation accepts any callable `createPlugin`, so a JavaScript provider can supply an async method. Its Promise is stored as though it were a plugin; if the factory throws, the rejection is never observed and can terminate the Node 22 Lambda invocation despite the documented isolation guarantee. Detect Promise-like results and either await them with rejection containment or attach a rejection handler and skip them. Add a unit test using a rejecting async factory.
